title: Negatives and Questions Quiz 3
description: Place have, has, been and the little words never, ever, yet and already correctly.
topic: Present perfect and present perfect continuous
instructions: Negatives and Questions: Present perfect and present perfect continuous.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Never goes between have and the past participle: I have never seen snow. Watch out: never does not go before have in a normal statement.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
options: Has she finished her homework yet?
Does she finished her homework yet?
Has she finish her homework yet?
Have she finished her homework yet?
questions.explanation: Present perfect question: Has + subject + past participle, with yet at the end. Watch out: does and have she do not fit the perfect.

questions.question: {{1}} you ever {{2}} (be) to Japan?
questions.explanation: Experience questions use Have + subject + ever + past participle. Watch out: the participle of be is been, not was.

questions.question: He {{1}} (not / call) me yet.
questions.explanation: Present perfect negative: has not + past participle, and yet goes at the end. Watch out: with he the helper is has, not have.

questions.question: 'I haven't never been there' is correct.
questions.explanation: A clause needs only one negative: I have never been there, or I haven't ever been there. Watch out: never already contains the negative.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: Yesterday is a finished time, so the past simple is needed: Did you eat yesterday? Watch out: a finished time word never goes with the present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative helper.

rows.given: He ___ finished the report so far.
They ___ arrived before the film started.

questions.explanation: Time clues decide the helper: since Monday and so far for the present perfect, before the film started for the past perfect, last year for the past simple, tomorrow for will. Watch out: have goes with I, has goes with he.

questions.question: Match each tense and form with its formula.
questions.explanation: The continuous forms add been before the verb-ing. Watch out: only have / has moves in the question, and been stays after the subject.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order to make a question.
questions.explanation: The question word comes first, then have, then the subject, then been waiting. Watch out: long stays with how.

questions.question: You want to know the length of time she has been in London. Which question is correct?
options: How long does she be in London?
How long has she been in London?
How long did she been in London?
How long is she been in London?
questions.explanation: A situation that continues up to now is asked with the perfect: How long has she been in London? Watch out: be never takes does or did.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct sentences use have / has + participle, or been + verb-ing. Watch out: Has you needs have, and saw is not a participle.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: Have you finished already your homework?
accepted: Have you already finished your homework?
Have you already finished your homework
Have you finished your homework already?
Have you finished your homework already
questions.explanation: Already goes after have, or at the end of the question. Watch out: it cannot come between the participle and its object.
